hallucinations.claim: `--media-control-bar-background` is a CSS custom property that styles the Mux Player control bar background
hallucinations.reality: This CSS variable is not part of Mux Player's public API and is not wired to any element in the default theme. The documented variable that affects the control bar backdrop is `--controls-backdrop-color`, and the supported way to target the bottom bar specifically is `::part(control-bar bottom)`.
hallucinations.evidence: Rung 3 edit added `style={{ "--media-control-bar-background": "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)" } as React.CSSProperties}` to <MuxPlayer>. Claude later confirmed via DOM probe: "--media-control-bar-background isn't actually wired to any element in Mux Player's default theme." Verified against the gerwig theme source in node_modules (no occurrence) and the Mux styles reference at https://www.mux.com/docs/guides/mux-player-web.

notes: Across the five rungs, Claude leaned heavily on empirical DOM probing rather than recalling API names from memory, which kept most claims grounded. The one factual hallucination was the CSS custom property `--media-control-bar-background`, used in Rung 3 as if it were a Mux Player styling hook; it does not exist (the documented analog is `--controls-backdrop-color`, and the bottom bar is targetable via `::part(control-bar bottom)`). Claude detected the mismatch via runtime inspection and recovered by switching to a `::part()` rule, so the final code does not contain the bad variable. Other props (`playbackId`, `muted`, `loop`, `autoPlay`, `thumbnailTime`, `accentColor`), imports (`@mux/mux-player-react`, type from `@mux/mux-player`), and ::part selectors used in `index.css` (seek-backward, seek-forward, playback-rate, audio-track, airplay, cast, control-bar top, control-bar bottom) match real part tokens emitted by the gerwig theme.
